criteria.criterion: US-015 valid monad.toml becomes a deterministic semantic document record.
criteria.evidence: Semantic config parser tests establish stable TOML source/document identity, exact content hash and byte length, deterministic canonical path, and repeatable serialized output.

criteria.criterion: US-016 schema/parse errors remain diagnostics and block a valid semantic config document.
criteria.evidence: Malformed TOML, duplicate keys, unknown keys, unsupported schema versions, invalid UTF-8, and stale effective state fail closed through structured diagnostics.

criteria.criterion: US-017 normalized semantic representation is deterministic and retains source/effective-value provenance distinctions.
criteria.evidence: Canonical file/default values remain distinct from CLI-effective values; ordered maps and serialization are deterministic.

criteria.criterion: .monad/manifest.yaml cannot override or become a competing semantic config source.
criteria.evidence: Legacy-manifest non-authority regression passes and serialized semantic state contains no manifest authority.

criteria.criterion: No environment interpolation, command substitution, network lookup, or include execution occurs.
criteria.evidence: Executable-looking and interpolation/include/network-like strings remain inert parser data in regression coverage.

criteria.criterion: Effective configuration is bound to the exact source bytes identified by the semantic document.
criteria.evidence: Rebound validation rejects stale or unrelated effective configuration for different monad.toml bytes.

criteria.criterion: Reliable TOML source ranges are retained for downstream diagnostics and provenance explanations.
criteria.evidence: Spanned TOML values are retained as deterministic semantic-path to byte-range mappings and verified against exact source slices.
